title: How agencies can find multi-location businesses
summary: Find multi-location business prospects, map buying responsibility, and build a focused agency offer.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


Marketing agencies can build a focused prospect list by combining business categories and locations with account research. Group branches under the right operator, check who controls marketing, and identify a public issue that your service can address.


- Choose one service offer and a business segment you can serve well.
- Confirm whether locations share a buyer or have separate franchise operators.
- Prepare a specific observation from the website before starting a conversation.


For an agency offering local SEO, paid media, or website services, a business with several locations can be a relevant prospect. But several addresses do not automatically mean one marketing budget. A franchise network may have separate operators, and a regional chain may buy centrally.


Build your list around the organization that can buy your service, then use location-level research to make the conversation specific.


## 1. Choose one offer and one business segment


Start with a concrete offer, such as improving location pages for regional auto repair groups. Define the region and the number of locations you can comfortably serve. A working segment might be operators with three to ten locations in one state; this is a test criterion, not a universal ideal customer profile.


Exclude businesses whose needs sit outside your offer. If you specialize in local SEO, a business without customer-facing locations may need a different service.


## 2. Find branches and group them into accounts


Begin with category and geography searches in[Openmart’s business database](https://www.openmart.com/products/local-business-database) . Use available profiles and websites to research possible multi-location operators.


Check the location directory on each business’s website. Record the shared brand, domain, and known locations. Similar names are not enough to establish common ownership.


For franchises, investigate who controls local marketing. Keep an unresolved ownership or budget question visible in your list rather than silently treating the whole brand as one buyer.


## 3. Audit one issue you can demonstrate


Review public location pages for inconsistent information, broken appointment links, or missing location-specific details. Record the page URL and a dated observation.


Reviews can add context, but a low rating does not prove a marketing problem. Nor does a public website reveal the business’s ad spend or willingness to change agencies. Use these observations to prepare questions.


## 4. Make the account list actionable


- **Brand and domain:** Avoid duplicate accounts
- **Locations and sources:** Establish the footprint
- **Operator structure:** Central, franchise, or unknown
- **Public issue:** Support a specific conversation
- **Marketing contact route:** Identify where to ask about responsibility
- **Offer fit:** Explain why your service is relevant


If you already have an account list,[business enrichment](https://www.openmart.com/products/local-business-enrichment) can help you research missing business details. Check which information is available for each account before relying on it.


## 5. Lead with a useful observation


For a practice example, suppose two location pages have broken appointment links. A relevant opening is: “I noticed the appointment links on two of your location pages lead to an error. Who handles updates across your locations? I can send the URLs.”


Use this only when the observation is real. Do not invent lost revenue or claim the business needs your agency before speaking with them.


Test 20 accounts. Track verified offer fit, conversations with the responsible team, and qualified opportunities. Expand the segment when those results justify it.


Use[Openmart](https://www.openmart.com/) to start the business research, then turn branch listings into a clear account map and a specific reason to talk.


## 6. Separate brand reach from buying responsibility


One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning’s[privacy policy](https://www.onehourheatandair.com/privacy-policy/) describes a network of separately owned and operated franchise locations. That disclosure is a reason to investigate the operator before assigning the whole brand to one agency prospect. It does not establish that marketing is decentralized, or that any location is looking for an agency.


- Brand: One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning.
- Public evidence: the brand describes franchise ownership at location level.
- Research decision: create operator-level accounts only after verifying the relationship.
- Still to confirm: local versus central marketing authority and the scope of services the operator can buy.


For your own pilot, retain a location sheet and a separate account sheet. Connect each location to a verified operator or an unresolved operator field. Count agencies’ potential customers at account level and count delivery workload at location level.[This deduplication workflow](https://www.openmart.com/blogs/deduplicate-multi-location-business-prospect-lists) explains how to handle the common exceptions.


Measure verified accounts, accounts with a demonstrated website issue, conversations with the responsible team, and qualified opportunities. A useful opportunity has an agreed problem, a relevant service scope, and a next step. A positive reply alone is not the same measure.


## Recommendation


Choose one vertical and region, then research 20 accounts. Use Openmart business profiles to begin your list, verify location relationships on company websites, and audit a specific issue relevant to your offer. Track qualified conversations with the responsible team before expanding.

## FAQs


**Do multiple locations share one marketing budget?**


Sometimes. Regional chains may buy centrally, while franchise locations may have separate operators. Confirm purchasing responsibility for each account.


**Which public signals are useful for agency prospecting?**


Broken links, inconsistent location details, and missing location-specific pages can support a concrete conversation when they relate to your service.


**Can business listings tell me the current agency or advertising budget?**


A listing alone does not establish either. Treat those details as questions for further research or discovery.
